title: Joining a tribe, including the anthropology student Finn
summary: Membership starts in the bar room and is often hereditary; one white Tulane student, Finn, joined the Black Eagles and wrote a paper.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How does one get into it? What is the criteria for entrance into a Mardi Gras, into one of the tribes?

Actually, it seems to be first you go to the bar room. Most of them do their practicing in the bar room. And it also has a hereditary factor that the tribe bring their children. You'll see children going along with their fathers from the age four years on up. And they just melt in and become part of the tribe. However, it is possible for, say, an outsider to become a member of the tribe.
Could you or I become, if you were, could you or I?

There is, there has been one Caucasian, a fellow from. Do they, is the color line very drawn? Yeah, but there has been one Caucasian, a fellow that was an anthropology student at Tulane. And I think he was either Swedish or Danish. His name was Finn. He joined the Black Eagles tribe. He wrote a paper on it and very interesting. And he, too, is a very interesting fellow.
I think that's what I, I mean, what research I did do. I think maybe that was what I was reading. Must have been his notes that he had made.
It probably was his notes. He wrote the first anthropologic paper that I've seen on it.
